# VaultScaler

> VaultScaler is edge computer-vision security for art. It builds private, on-premise security systems for galleries, museums, and private collections. The intelligence runs on hardware the customer owns, in their building; nothing it sees ever leaves the room, and nothing is ever attached to the artwork. Bespoke and consulting-led — specified, built, installed, and tuned in person. Based in the Las Vegas Arts District; works internationally. Founded in 2025.

VaultScaler's approach has three parts. At the edge: the system runs on a box in the customer's building — no cloud, no account, nothing phoned home. There is no server for anyone to subpoena, breach, or browse, because there isn't a server. Honest by design: the system knows the difference between a person standing in front of a painting and a painting that is no longer there — so it does not cry wolf, and the alarms mean something. Owned end to end: VaultScaler builds and trains its own computer vision on its own hardware; the intelligence is theirs, not rented from a platform that can change its terms or cut them off.

## The three problems VaultScaler exists to fix

1. Cloud camera systems put a gallery's footage, collectors, and transactions on infrastructure the owner does not control — viewable by strangers and reachable by anyone who breaches it. For a business built on discretion, that is the risk, not a feature.
2. Conventional object protection cannot tell a visitor leaning in to look from a work being lifted off the wall. The false alarms are constant, so institutions quietly disconnect them. A system nobody trusts is a system nobody uses.
3. Traditional protection puts hardware on the art — tags behind canvases, laser curtains, contacts and vibration sensors on the frame. It touches the work, constrains the hang, and tells every visitor the art is wired.

## What the system does

- Nothing leaves the building: intelligence runs on owned hardware on-premise; no cloud, no account, nothing phoned home — as an architecture, not a policy.
- It knows the difference: it understands a person in front of a work versus a work that is gone. Admiring the work does not trigger an alarm; removing it does. This distinction is the hardest problem in the field and the one built for first.
- Nothing touches the artwork: the camera watches; the work hangs unwired, untagged, unconstrained. Rehang the room whenever you like and the system is re-taught in minutes.
- Fewer guards, better cover: it watches every piece at once, without breaks; it does not replace staff but means fewer are needed, and they know exactly where to go.

## What it sees

- Every work, individually — draw a boundary around each piece; the system learns what that wall looks like with the work on it.
- Removal — if a work leaves its place, you know within seconds.
- Contact — if someone reaches into a piece, you know immediately.
- People — recognise staff, regulars, and collectors and flag unknown people; or run fully anonymous with every face obscured before it is ever stored. The owner's building, rules, and call.
- A record you can use — every event, timestamped, with an image: who was where, when, and what they touched.
- Open hours and closed hours — the system knows a busy opening from an empty room at 3am and behaves accordingly.

## How VaultScaler works (a consultancy, not a shipment)

1. Come and look — walk the room; assess the light, flow, hang, and what is actually at risk.
2. Design for the room — a system specified for the building and collection, not a package.
3. Build it — the computer vision is built and trained by VaultScaler on its own hardware.
4. Install and tune it — installation by a licensed contractor, then tuning in person until the false alarms are gone and the system reports only what matters.
5. It's yours — the customer owns the hardware and the footage; no mandatory subscription; it keeps working with no further contact.

## Who it's for

Commercial galleries, private collections, artist-run and independent spaces, small museums and institutions — anyone whose business depends on discretion.

## Where VaultScaler is

Based in the Las Vegas Arts District, running its own exhibition space with the system installed and watching its own work. Works internationally; the architecture is the same everywhere (local, owned, nothing leaving the building), configured to the law of each jurisdiction — the highest security available within the customer's legal framework.
